subject: Benchmark reproducibility playbook & streaming SLO checklist
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole, ben_carter
Date: 2027-06-21T15:02:00Z
Subject: Benchmark reproducibility playbook & streaming SLO checklist

Hi Alice — great call earlier today, thanks for walking us through the integration surface. Quick written recap and proposed artifacts so we can get your perf/QoS questions into a reproducible test.

Recap (high level):
- Goal: validate that Redwood meets Acme's streaming and conversational SLOs under realistic concurrency for the Checkout assistant.
- Primary SLOs discussed: P95 latency <= 120ms (tail policy for production), P99 <= 400ms for short responses, sustained throughput target 200 reqs/s per slot, graceful degradation for concurrency spikes to 800 concurrent streams.
- Streaming requirement: 95% of tokens should begin streaming within 40ms of generation start; end-to-end completion time measured separately (see definitions below).

Artifacts attached: prompt_set_v1.json (seed prompts reflecting top 50 user intents), a small sample trace (streaming_sample_trace.txt) from our internal run.

Proposed next steps (owner / ETA):
1) Marissa: send formal measurement definitions and reproducibility steps (tomorrow EOD).
2) We (Redwood): provide harness instructions and a Dockerized harness tarball for your eng team to run in your environment (expected Wed).
3) Acme: run a smoke harness run against your staging bucket with our prompt_set_v1 and share logs (you said availability earliest Thu-Fri this week).
4) Joint 60-min test window next week to run a full qualification and collect KV cache / cold start traces (propose Tue 10:00am PT).

Acceptance criteria (draft):
- P95 latency (end-to-end, warmed cache) <= 120ms across 15-minute steady-state run at target throughput.
- Token streaming start time median < 40ms.
- No more than 1% request failures (5xx or timeouts).

Questions to confirm from your side:
- Is there an absolute hard P99 limit we should be aware of for SLAs?
- Can you share a sample of your request size distribution (tokens per prompt) or confirm it aligns with prompt_set_v1?

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.json (seed prompts), streaming_sample_trace.txt (sample trace).

Thanks — I’ll coordinate scheduling once Marissa shares the measurement doc.

— Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com

From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@acme.com>

Cc: Acme EngPerf <eng+perf@acme.com>, marissa_cole
Date: 2027-06-21T16:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Benchmark reproducibility playbook & streaming SLO checklist

Thanks Ava — good summary. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the prompt bundle: 

1) P99 SLA: we don't have a hard P99 SLA for the pilot, but production threshold target for the business is P99 <= 600ms. If you can show consistent P95 <= 120ms and P99 <= 600ms on the qualification we should be fine to proceed to a pilot.
2) Request size distribution: our median is ~42 tokens (user prompt) and 75 tokens combined average response length for Checkout flows; worst-case tails hit ~400 tokens for verbose troubleshooting. The prompt_set_v1 sample looks close but please confirm how you account for the 400-token tail in batching and cost estimates.
3) Cold-starts: we need a clear definition for cold vs warmed runs. For us, "cold" should be when the model has not seen any requests for 30m and has an empty KV cache. Can you provide a cold-start test in the harness?

Also: we prefer to run the harness in our VPC — can you provide the Docker image + script and a deterministic RNG seed so we can reproduce exactly? Please include any environment variables required.

I can do Thu-Fri for a smoke run, and Tue next week works for the joint window.

— Alice
Senior Product Lead, Acme Enterprises
alice.turner@acme.com

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@acme.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter, kimberly_park
Date: 2027-06-22T09:33:00Z
Subject: Re: Benchmark reproducibility playbook & streaming SLO checklist

Hi Alice — following up with the measurement definitions and a reproducibility checklist. I've kept these intentionally concrete so your EngPerf team can run the harness in your VPC and compare logs verbatim with our run. Attachment: harness_instructions.md (contains commands).

Measurement definitions (canonical):
- Request: a single API call containing prompt + metadata.
- Token streaming start time: time from request receipt at edge ingress to first bytes emitted to client. Measured in ms; report median, P95, P99.
- End-to-end latency (response completion): time from request receipt to final token flush. Report median, P95, P99.
- Warmed run: KV cache primed for identical prompt fingerprints; run defined as "warmed" after a 5-minute warmup at target throughput with same prompt distribution.
- Cold run: no prior requests for 30 minutes and cold runtime (containers restarted, KV empty). We will support automated container recycle in the harness.
- Concurrency: number of simultaneous open streaming connections. Sustained concurrency target is 200; burst test up to 800 for graceful degradation validation.

Reproducibility checklist (run order):
1) Pull harness image and verify sha256 (we'll provide).
2) Seed RNG (HARNESS_SEED) to the supplied seed value.
3) Run cache empty script (./harness/clear_kv.sh) and confirm emptiness.
4) Execute cold-run profile: 1000 requests spread over 10m, capture raw traces.
5) Execute warmup: 5 minutes at target throughput (200 reqs/s).
6) Execute warmed steady-state run: 15 minutes at 200 reqs/s; collect token-level timestamps and upstream GPU telemetry.
7) Execute burst/concurrency ramp: ramp from 200 -> 800 concurrent streams over 2 minutes and hold 2 minutes.
8) Upload artifacts: raw traces, aggregate metrics, and a sanitized trace sample to the shared Drive link.

What we will provide:
- harness_instructions.md (attached) with exact CLI commands and env var list.
- Docker image name + sha256 and a lightweight runner script for VPC execution.
- Example flag set for canary config (batching disabled vs enabled) so you can validate cost/latency trade-offs.

Acceptance criteria (explicit):
- WARMED P95 <= 120ms across 15-minute steady state.
- WARMED token streaming start median < 40ms.
- COLD median degradation not exceeding 3x warmed P95 (for traceability).
- Burst failure rate < 3% and graceful rate-limiting events logged.

I can share the harness link by EOD. If this looks good, Ava — can you confirm scheduling and who from Acme will own the smoke run?

— Marissa Cole
Sr. Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
